diagnostic_evidence.quote: The improved noise dependence to $\frac{n}{m}\|\sigma\|^2_{L^2_\nu}$ can be obtained for free by performing the same estimates above \cite[Eq. (4.5)]{cohen2017optimal} without the last inequality.
Thus, \eqref{newb} improves the bound in Theorem \ref{thm:cm17} in terms of sample complexity.

issues.failure_explanation: The variance of the weighted least-squares estimator with Christoffel weights, computed exactly as in the paper's own derivation of \eqref{lo904}, is (up to the conditioning constant) \frac{1}{m}\int w^2\sigma^2\Phi_n\,d\nu = \frac{1}{m}\int w\sigma^2\Phi_n\,d\mu = \frac{n}{m}\|\sigma\|^2_{L^2_\mu}, since w\Phi_n = n. The theorem instead states \frac{n}{m}\|\sigma\|^2_{L^2_\nu} = \frac{n}{m}\int \sigma^2\Phi_n/n\,d\mu, an incomparable quantity that can be much smaller (when \sigma is concentrated where \Phi_n is small), so the stated bound is not what the cited argument yields and is false in general. Remark rem:compare then compares \eqref{newb} to this incorrect baseline via Jensen.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace \|\sigma\|^2_{L^2_\nu} by \|\sigma\|^2_{L^2_\mu} in thm:cm17 and the introduction; in Remark rem:compare replace the Jensen step by Cauchy–Schwarz (\|\sigma\sqrt{\Phi_n/n}\|_{L^1_\mu} \le \|\sigma\|_{L^2_\mu}), which also absorbs the \frac{1}{m}\|\sigma\|^2_{L^2_\mu} term, so the improvement claim survives.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:cm17 as stated is incorrect; the introduction's sample-complexity discussion (m \gtrsim n\max\{\log n, \eta^{-1}\|\sigma\|^2_{L^2_\nu}\}) and the comparison in Remark rem:compare rest on the wrong baseline term. The paper's own bounds (thm:main) are unaffected.
issues.title: Noise term in Theorem thm:cm17 has the wrong norm (L^2_nu instead of L^2_mu)
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the background theorem's norm and a one-line change in the comparison restore all of the paper's substantive claims; no result of the paper is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: there exists a direction $\bm a = (a_1, \ldots, a_m)^\top$ supported on $\text{supp}_{\delta}(\bm q^{*}_n)$ such that  $\sum_{i\in [m]}\frac{a_i}{\sigma^2(x_i)}R_iR^\top_i = 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The direction a only guarantees U(q+ta) = U(q); it does not guarantee \|q+ta\|_1 = 1, so q+ta need not lie in P_m(\delta). The dimension count (more than n(n+1)/2 rank-one matrices are dependent) does not yield \sum_i a_i = 0. An additional argument is needed: if \sum_i a_i \ne 0, rescaling (q+ta)/(1+t\sum a_i) with t\sum a_i<0 is feasible and strictly lowers H (by homogeneity of U), contradicting optimality, so \sum a_i = 0 for every null direction at an optimum; this step is missing.

failure_location.quote: Applying a perturbation argument for $\bm q^{*}_n$ along $\bm a$ yields another optimal solution that has a smaller $\delta$-support.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the optimality/homogeneity argument showing that any null direction at an optimum satisfies \sum_i a_i = 0, then perform the perturbation within the simplex.
issues.overall_effect: The sparsity bound \eqref{spt} is not fully justified as written; the convexity/existence part of the lemma and its use in Algorithm alg:1 are unaffected.
issues.title: Sparsity argument in Lemma mkjh ignores the simplex constraint along the perturbation direction
issues.why_classification: A short, contained argument fills the gap and the stated bound survives unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \leq&\  \|(\bm V^\top\bm W\bm V)^{-1}\|_2^2\cdot\E_{\bm y}[\|\bm V^\top\bm W^{\frac{1}{2}}(\bm y-\bm f)\|_2^2\mid \XX]\nonumber\\

issues.failure_explanation: Gauss–Markov gives H(p) <= Var of the non-reweighted estimator, and the paper only shows this variance is <= \|(V^T W V)^{-1}\|_2^2 G(p) (eq1); G(p) itself is not the unweighted variance. Hence H(p_n^*) <= G(p_n^*) does not follow, and the unconditional inequality \E_X[H(q_n^*)] <= \E_X[G(p_n^*)] is unsupported since \|(V^T W V)^{-1}\|_2 is unbounded over X. Only a constant-factor version conditional on the event A (where the factor is <= (1/0.81)^2) is justified.

failure_location.quote: so that $H(\bm q^{*}_n)\leq H(\bm p^*_n)\leq G(\bm p^*_n)$ (the first inequality follows from the definition of $\bm q_n^*$ and the second uses the Gauss--Markov theorem), which implies $\E_\XX[H(\bm q^{*}_n)]\leq \E_\XX[G(\bm p^*_n)]$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the comparison conditional on A with the factor \|(V^T W V)^{-1}\|_2^2 <= (1/0.81)^2, i.e. \E_X[H(q_n^*)|A] \lesssim \E_X[G(p_n^*)|A].
issues.overall_effect: The claimed variance advantage of the reweighted allocation in Remark rem:compare is only established up to a constant and conditional on A; the theorem bounds themselves are unaffected.
issues.title: Remark rem:compare: H(p_n^*) <= G(p_n^*) via Gauss–Markov is unsupported without the conditioning factor
issues.why_classification: The qualitative comparison survives with a constant factor and conditioning; no theorem changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Choosing $l\geq \log(1/\delta)/\log 2$ and noting $2/\log 2<3$ yields the desired result.

issues.failure_explanation: The boosting argument needs l = \lceil \log_2(1/\delta) \rceil disjoint blocks of size k, i.e. n >= k\lceil \log_2(1/\delta)\rceil. The hypothesis n > 1.5\log(1/\delta)k does not imply this: e.g. \delta slightly below 1/4 gives l = 3 but 1.5\log(1/\delta) \approx 2.1, and for \delta \in (1/2,1) the hypothesis can allow n < k so no block fits. The proof therefore does not cover the theorem's stated parameter range.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the hypothesis by n >= k\lceil \log_2(1/\delta) \rceil (or n > (1.5\log(1/\delta)+1)k).
issues.overall_effect: The probability guarantee of thm:rb is unproven for many values of \delta (those just below powers of 1/2 and \delta close to 1); the result holds with a slightly larger constant.
issues.title: Theorem thm:rb: hypothesis n > 1.5 log(1/delta) k does not accommodate the integer number of blocks used in the proof
issues.why_classification: Only the explicit constant in the hypothesis changes; the result and its rate survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the last step holds if choosing $s = c'r(\log r)^3$, where $c'>0$ is some sufficiently large absolute constant (independent of $r$).

issues.failure_explanation: For r = 1, (\log r)^3 = 0 so k = 0 and s = 0, whereas the proof requires s > 2r+1 and a block of size 2s <= k; the statement then asserts \min_{v\in\{0\}}\|f-v\| = \|f\|_{L^2_\mu} <= 24\sqrt{\tau_2}, which is false in general (e.g. \lambda_2 = 0, f \ne 0). Similarly, when 10\log(1/\delta) < 1 (\delta > e^{-0.1}) the hypothesis permits n < k, so not even one block of the boosting argument fits, and the ceiling \lceil \log(1/\delta)/\log(10/9)\rceil is not always covered by 10\log(1/\delta).

failure_location.quote: with $k = \lceil C_1 r(\log r)^3\rceil$ and for any $\delta>0$, if $n> 10\log (1/\delta) k$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (\log r)^3 by (\log(r+1))^3 (or require r >= 2 and let C_1 absorb small-r cases) and state the hypothesis as n >= k\lceil \log(1/\delta)/\log(10/9) \rceil (or n > (10\log(1/\delta)+1)k).
issues.overall_effect: The theorem as stated is false at r = 1 and unproven for \delta close to 1; the substantive content for r >= 2 and moderate \delta is unaffected.
issues.title: Theorem thm:984 fails in degenerate parameter regimes (r = 1 gives k = 0; small log(1/delta) does not ensure a block fits)
issues.why_classification: Degenerate-case and constant adjustments only; the approximation rate and main regime survive intact.
